target_customer: iPhone owners who wanted short, social workouts and paid 0.99 dollars for the app
problem: People struggle to stay motivated to exercise. FitFu used the iPhone accelerometer to count short exercises and rewarded them with points, levels and friend challenges.
business_model: Paid iOS app at 0.99 dollars per download with a free social network

founders.name: Jof Arnold
founders.background_notes: Named by TNW as the founder who explained the 2012 shutdown. No education or prior employers found in opened sources.

founders.name: Benjie Gillam
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page with no bio.

exit.reason: The team said the money had run dry. The app was removed from sale on September 18, 2012 and the social network was due to close on October 31, 2012. Jof Arnold blamed the App Store for weak income even at the top of the Health and Fitness chart.

competitors.name: Git Fit
competitors.what: iPhone app that made workout stats visible to friends for social pressure

competitors.name: Nexercise
competitors.what: Free iPhone game that rewards people for exercising consistently

competitors.name: Fit Friendzy (MedHelp and GE)
competitors.what: App where friends compete in over fifty exercise challenges

technical_complexity.rationale: Accelerometer based rep detection on iPhone plus a points and social layer. Detection tuning was the hard part, but it was standard mobile engineering for 2010 to 2011.

defensibility.rationale: A paid app with eight exercises and a points system could be cloned in weeks, and the friend network was small.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it. The company closed in September 2012 after running out of money, and Arnold blamed App Store economics.

market_need_then: Fitness and gamification apps were a hot iPhone category in 2011, with many launches (Git Fit, Nexercise, Fit Friendzy, Fitocracy online in early 2011). TNW in March 2011 said the friend challenge idea was not seen in other apps.

branding.name_origin: Described by TNW as an evolution of the earlier PushupFu app. The meaning of Fu is not explained in any opened source.
branding.domain_note: fitfu.com did not load during research (HTTP 503). A different company, FiTFU Lyfe LLC, holds a FITFU clothing trademark filed in 2020.

identity.voice_and_tone: Three stated principles: Perseverance, Progress and Being Friendly (TNW, March 2011)

branding.community_and_virality: TNW covered the launch in March 2011 and the closure in 2012. No merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Press coverage at launch and at shutdown, and a top ranking in Health and Fitness at some point, but no evidence of a lasting brand asset.

outcome_analysis: FitFu launched in late 2010 as a 0.99 dollar iPhone app and reached the top of Health and Fitness, but its founders said the income was too low and the money ran out. The app was pulled from sale on September 18, 2012. The founder blamed the App Store, and the one dollar price meant revenue depended on huge volume. No outside funding was found.
notes: No funding rounds found in press or in database searches (searches returned only similarly named companies). TNW dates are from the article text; the closing article year (2012) is inferred from the September 18 Tuesday date in the search summary and the article text in the fetch. Nexercise source is dated 2011 by URL only. Fit Friendzy is a July 2011 source, a few months after the W11 batch. The website returned HTTP 503 and could not be read.
